issue.title: "MAVSDK" and "Arducopter SITL" incompatibility (and fly_qgc_mission.cpp and QGC incompatibility)
issue.body:
Hi,

I'm the current maintainer of [Rosetta Drone 3](https://github.com/The1only/rosettadrone), a MAVLink implementation for DJI drones.
We are testing MAVSDK to send a QGC mission to [Arducopter SITL](https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/MissionPlanner/sitl/) using `fly_qgc_mission.cpp`.
We identified at least two issues:

- ISSUE 1: `telemetry.health_all_ok()` is always `false`
- ISSUE 2: Arducopter doesn't start the mission but disarms.

Everything works fine sending the mission from QGC to Arducopter SITL instead of using `fly_qgc_mission.cpp`.

```
Output of fly_qgc_mission.cpp:

	Waiting to discover system...
	Discovered autopilot
	Waiting for system to be ready	<--- BUG 1: blocks on while (!telemetry.health_all_ok())
	(Waiting disabled by me, for testing)
	System ready
	Importing mission from mission plan: /data/data/com.termux/files/home/imatronix/server/test/p9-quillota.plan
	Found 10 mission items in the given QGC plan.
	Uploading mission...Mission uploaded.
	Arming...
	Armed.
	

Output of arducopter.exe:

	...
	AP: EKF3 IMU0 is using GPS
	AP: EKF3 IMU1 is using GPS
	AP: Terrain: clamping offset 435 to 15
	AP: Arming motors
	ARMED
	Mode AUTO
	AP: Mission: 1 Takeoff
	waypoint 1
	
	(little pause, probably a timeout)
	
	AP: Disarming motors	<--- BUG 2: Unexpected disarm. Why? There is no problem when sending the same mission from QGC
	AP: Mission: 1 Takeoff
	DISARMED
```

Are this incompatibilities intentional?
How do we make this world better?

IMO `fly_qgc_mission.cpp` is suposed to send QGC missions, so I would expect it to speak the same language as QGC (or rename it to `fly_qgc_mission_in_unintelligible_accent.cpp`).

comments.body:
Regarding the health fields: that was just some proxy that I came up with which tended to work ok with PX4. It's not properly done as it should. It should probably depend on the `health.is_armable` flag instead which is basically [MAV_SYS_STATUS_PREARM_CHECK](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#MAV_SYS_STATUS_PREARM_CHECK).
It would probably be a good idea to remove the `health_is_all_ok` in MAVSDK v2 and recommend `is_armable` everywhere.

Now when it comes to missions that's a bit harder because various items get interpreted differently, and then the mission transfer is also different, ArduPilot putting home into item 0 and starting with item 1 for the mission while PX4 just starts at 0.

For your exact problem, I'm not sure what exactly it is, but let's try to debug it and fix it.

> Are this incompatibilities intentional?

No, just the way things were standardized appropriately or interpreted differently and have developed from there.

> How do we make this world better?

There is a two-weekly MAVLink dev call where we discuss what gets added to MAVLink and how PX4 and ArduPilot can slowly become more compatible. However, progress is hard, because often to become more compatible requires changes which would break backwards compatibility or additions of new mechanisms which require implementing or add complexity.

But anyway, let's debug what you're stuck on and go from there.

Any chance you can provide me code or steps how I can reproduce the issue?

Thanks @julianoes,

I got `fly_qgc_mission.cpp` working with Arducopter SIT.
I had to disable the `telemetry.health_all_ok()` and set `AUTO_OPTIONS` = 10 in Arducopter SITL.
More info [here](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/22966).

But this was just the initial test.
Where I really need help is in getting MAVSDK / `fly_qgc_mission.cpp` to work with Rosetta, which already works fine with QGC.
I will create an issue here: https://github.com/The1only/rosettadrone/issues/120

Hi @kripper, nice work with Rosettadrone! 
I think QGC mission from a file would not work as it is. This is because APM expects slightly different mission sequences. As a side not, APM expects first mission item as the home position and second mission item as takeoff. QGC does this conversion when uploading the mission to the autopilot but the example file you mentioned does not.

Please use the [MAVSDK integration tests](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/main/src/integration_tests/mission_raw_import_and_fly.cpp) as basis for mission upload to APM SITL. There are two separate tests in this file, one each for PX4 and APM.

See how mission upload, arm and takeoff are executed in a sequence to run the mission with APM in this function: [APM Mission Raw Integration test](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/d3115f547f8a7dee4b6c61dea1211ca80101d4b9/src/integration_tests/mission_raw_import_and_fly.cpp#L90)

Also see how the mission plan is created in [Create Mission Plan Raw for APM](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/d3115f547f8a7dee4b6c61dea1211ca80101d4b9/src/integration_tests/mission_raw_import_and_fly.cpp#L151)

Hope this helps :)

Best,
khedar

> It would probably be a good idea to remove the `health_is_all_ok` in MAVSDK v2 and recommend `is_armable` everywhere.

Yes. Having a universal `is_armable` check that each fight controller knows how to interpret depending on their features and sensors is a good idea.

BTW, when sending the first mission from QGC, we get an error saying that the aircraft is unable to arm even when it 1) sends the ACK to the arm/disarm command, 2) send the ACK to the set-flight-mode command and 3) informs that the flight mode is GUIDED in the next heartbeat.

I think I have seen this also once with arducopter SITL.

I believe QGC then disables the arming check and it works the second time...or we switch the fight mode to auto to get Rosetta actually starting the mission.

This only happens with QGC. With the C++ example, the mission starts flawlessly. Anyway, we should better fix this issue with QGC.

> Now when it comes to missions that's a bit harder because various items get interpreted differently, and then the mission transfer is also different, ArduPilot putting home into item 0 and starting with item 1 for the mission while PX4 just starts at 0.

I don't see a problem if the first item is a set-home-location or a take-off. 
All models can and should support both sequences.

> There is a two-weekly MAVLink dev call where we discuss what gets added to MAVLink and how PX4 and ArduPilot can slowly become more compatible. However, progress is hard, because often to become more compatible requires changes which would break backwards compatibility or additions of new mechanisms which require implementing or add complexity.

Good. On the long term, it pays off.

Congratulations. I admire your work on QGC.
Tomorrow I'll try to replay some logs with QGC.
I was looking for a debugging tool for Rosetta''s ground based "fight controller" (MissionManager) that uses virtual sticks to fly the missions.
I experienced an issue that didn't occur in the simulator, so the logs are crucial.

> BTW, when sending the first mission from QGC, we get an error saying that the aircraft is unable to arm even when it 1) sends the ACK to the arm/disarm command, 2) send the ACK to the set-flight-mode command and 3) informs that the flight mode is GUIDED in the next heartbeat.

I think I see something similar often with PX4 but I never quite tried to get to the bottom of it. Or at least it's a similar "try again and it works on the second try" sort of thing.

Yes, it's like a first time timeout. I believe I've also seen a message saying something like "arm check disabled".
I believe this is on the QGC side.

issue.title: Adding support for ArduPilot

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
## Context

A while ago, @peterbarker worked on adding support for APM in the SDK ([here](https://github.com/peterbarker/DroneCore/tree/ardupilot)). More recently, @jinchengde (and others) started looking into that, again. The goal of this issue is to discuss the high-level requirements and architecture.

## Benefits for APM

The project is architectured in such a way that everything relies on a C++ MAVLink implementation. Making this implementation compatible with APM means that APM will also get the language bindings ([Python](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-python), [Swift](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-swift), [Java](https://github.com/dronecore/dronecore-java) and future ones like [Javascript](https://github.com/mrpollo/DronecodeSDK-JavaScript)).

The interface common to all our bindings is defined [here](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK-Proto/tree/master/protos) and is used to auto-generate language-specific APIs (e.g. using RxSwift in Swift, RxJava in Java, and asyncio in Python).

## SDK architecture (overview)

The SDK can been seen as composed from 4 parts:

1. The [interface definition](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK-Proto/tree/master/protos) (protobuf files), common to all the languages (C++, Swift, Java, Python). Each proto file is considered a "plugin", which is a group of (MAVLink) features.
2. The C++ [MAVLink implementation](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK), which actually maintains a connection to the drone and does the MAVLink logic.
3. The [backend](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/tree/develop/backend), which exposes the C++ implementation of (2) as a messaging server through the interface of (1).
4. The language bindings ([Python](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-python), [Swift](https://github.com/dronecode/dronecodesdk-swift), [Java](https://github.com/dronecore/dronecore-java)), which implement (1) to communicate with the backend (3).

At the lowest level, each plugin (defined by one proto file) is a C++ library. The backend uses those libraries, as can been seen [here](https://github.com/Dronecode/DronecodeSDK/blob/develop/backend/src/CMakeLists.txt#L38-L46).

issue.title: Ardupilot and MAVSDK compatability

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
# Bug report

Greetings. I am trying to communicate with ArduCopter firmware via MAVSDK, and i found out a few problems. Some of them already discussed in #1990 issue.

**Issue details**

1. action.takeoff() implementation for apm - [takeoff_async_apm](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/blob/ab24200b9df9176890ec5e80c332708ba72d2a59/src/mavsdk/plugins/action/action_impl.cpp#L387)  function works only if vehicle is not in offboard mode. This is kinda strange behaviour. e.g. User might change mode to offboard via rc controller and then want to takeoff, but in this case command would not be sent.
Probably there is missing else branch.

2. Another strange thing, not a bug, but misleading behavior is telemetry.set_rate_battery(). This function sets MAVLINK_MSG_ID_SYS_STATUS, which is used not only for battery, but for health status primarily. Probably this function should be called set_rate_sys_status()? And for battery rate MAVSDK should implement set_rate_battery(), which sets [BATTERY_STATUS](https://mavlink.io/en/messages/common.html#BATTERY_STATUS) rate?

issue.title: QGC fails to take off the first time with "failed to arm" error

repository.name: rosettadrone
repository.description: MAVlink and H.264 Video for DJI drones

issue.body:
### Describe the bug

QGC fails to take off the first time with "failed to arm" error

### Workaround

Set mode in QGC to "Auto" and retry take off.

### What we know

See: https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/1990

Every implementation is doing different arming checks and Rosetta probably is not passing them.

Feel free to add more messages to Rosetta to improve compatibility with more MAVLink implementations.

### Steps To Reproduce

* Restart drone, RosettaDrone and QGC
* take off in QGC

issue.title: Add upload_mission_with_progress_async for mission_raw class

repository.name: MAVSDK
repository.description: API and library for MAVLink compatible systems written in C++ 20

issue.body:
Adds `MissionRaw::upload_mission_with_progress_async`. Mirrors the existing method for Mission class.

Tested on PX4 SITL (full mission with progress display) and ArduPilot SITL(Mission upload progress success). Mission execution on ArduPilot won't run, probably related to #1990.

Depends on this [Proto PR](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK-Proto/pull/406).
